claims.statement: The LangSmith agent documentation model is that a workspace contains agents, an agent’s traces are divided among the fixed Production, Staging, Development, and Local environments, and every trace records an agent and one environment; an identifier is immutable while a display name can change.

Agent trace addressing requires an identifier and environment together: explicit code configuration takes precedence, environment variables are used only when neither code destination is supplied, and a partial variable pair warns and leaves otherwise unaddressed calls untraced.

Agent registration is a one-time setup operation that requires a credential with projects:create rather than a tracing key; the creation response exposes each environment’s tracer_session_name and tracer_session_id, and an existing identifier returns 409.

An agent environment’s returned tracer_session_name is the compatibility value for integrations requiring a project name, while its tracer_session_id or resolved session_id is used by APIs with project_id or project_ids fields; these values must be read from the environment rather than derived from an agent name.

Agent addressing cannot be combined with legacy project destination settings: conflicting agent and legacy variables prevent otherwise unaddressed tracing, an explicit address plus project_name errors, and ingestion rejects requests with both address types.

For OpenTelemetry agent routing, OTLP requests must carry both Langsmith-Agent-Id and Langsmith-Agent-Environment headers; the Python exporter derives them from agent variables only when OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS is unset, while partial or mixed project-and-agent requests are rejected with 400 and span attributes do not route a trace to an agent.

mda dev compiles and runs an MDA project locally without creating a hosted deployment, and its Local-environment traces are rejected in agent-based workspaces until the matching agent record exists; mda deploy creates the hosted Agent Server deployment and routes context, source, secrets, and schedules through distinct deployment steps.

The Python, TypeScript, and Java trace-routing samples are marked runnable sources that respectively use ls.agent_address in decorators or tracing_context, AgentAddress in traceable configuration, and AgentAddress in a TraceConfig builder; remove-marked blocks retain validation outside rendered snippets.

OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT is a base URL to which OTLP HTTP exporters append /v1/traces, whereas OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT is used exactly as supplied; focused tests prohibit a generic endpoint with a signal suffix and verify both endpoint forms resolve without a duplicate suffix.

mda dev creates a local build, local Context Hub mock, language-specific LangGraph development server, and Studio session; local identity, temporary sandbox fallback, and non-provisioned schedules are development-only defaults that differ from a deployed agent.

Generated code snippets are produced by the code-snippets target from source markers, while test-code-samples executes selected runnable sources; traced multi-snippet sources are intentionally excluded from public trace-link publication.

Managed Deep Agents projects have one required root agent entry, while selected paths such as identity, memory, channels, schedules, tools/mcp, and sandbox enable managed capabilities; instructions.md and skills/ are synchronized as managed Context Hub content.

MDA deployment maps project inputs to distinct hosted surfaces: instructions and skills go to Context Hub, source is archived from .mda/build, non-reserved environment values become hosted secrets, and schedules are reconciled only after the deployment is live; --no-wait skips schedule reconciliation.

The onboarding model checker is a read-only monitor of external langchain-ai/langchainplus snippets: its YAML registry declares the repository, ref, paths, provider current and preferred IDs, and ignores, while the checker reports outdated IDs without editing the external files and exits 0 for clean input, 1 for findings, or 2 for unreadable input.

The onboarding model check runs on a weekly schedule or manually with read-only external-repository access, publishes its report, and opens, updates, or closes a standing GitHub issue for stale models rather than modifying the external snippets.

Focused onboarding-model tests cover provider-prefix detection, dated snapshots, false-positive and ignore handling, safe source validation, local-checkout reads, registry validity, and clean or stale exit behavior.
